title: Laws of stoichiometry
notes: **Law of conservation of mass.** Lavoisier: matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction, so total reactant mass equals total product mass.

**Law of definite proportions.** Proust: a pure compound always contains the same elements in the same fixed proportion by mass, whatever its source — water is always 11.1% hydrogen and 88.9% oxygen by mass.

**Law of multiple proportions.** Dalton: when two elements form several compounds, the masses of one combining with a fixed mass of the other stand in simple whole-number ratios — CO and CO₂ contain 16 g and 32 g oxygen per 12 g carbon.
**Gay-Lussac's law of gaseous volumes.** Gaseous reactants and products at the same temperature and pressure combine in simple whole-number ratios of volume.
**Avogadro's law.** Equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules, which explains Gay-Lussac's volume ratios.
